item.text: {"decisions":[{"decision":"accept","item_id":"feed:cursor:301c1497d14b1ed17100","piece_ids":["01","03"],"reason":"The in-window announcement provides usable shipment facts: Cursor says Rollouts creates editable monitoring plans and can alert, pause a rollout, or prepare a revert PR, while Security Reviewer supplies attack paths and proposed fixes. Moving agents into deployment and security controls is novel and highly relevant to small teams, although telemetry integration and Teams/Enterprise availability limit fit. Cursor sells these products; no method, cases, precision/recall, incident outcomes, or rollback-reliability data support its effectiveness claims, and the duplicated excerpt is not corroboration. Use 01 for what shipped and 03 for a permission-limited pilot with human approval, not as proof of safety." ,"version_id":"v-9e5e5fac9d48014feb9c5bfc"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"feed:cursor:84d2e8f0655374a11ab2","piece_ids":["02","03"],"reason":"This is unusually specific vendor evidence about harness engineering: production-traffic A/B testing, a reported 7% overall token-cost reduction, scoped savings from dynamic tool loading, caching, and sparser line numbers, plus an explicit subagent coordination tax. Those observations are novel and actionable for small teams managing long-running-agent cost and context. Cursor benefits both commercially and operationally from portraying its harness as efficient; sample sizes, test duration, distributions, the quality measure, and several denominators are missing, so all figures must remain vendor-reported—especially the 46.9% result limited to sessions invoking MCP. It is distinct from Cursor’s product-bot launch. Use 02 to scrutinize the measurements and 03 to motivate local cost, latency, cache-hit, error, and coordination tracking.","version_id":"v-5fed8f79222f91b61985792d"},{"decision":"reject","item_id":"feed:github:7a6dc2d18f9ec533b042","piece_ids":[],"reason":"The usable facts are limited to Gemini 4 Argon’s Copilot availability, gradual rollout, eligible plans, administrator controls, and provider-list billing. Claims that it solved more tasks on every benchmark and thoroughly checks edge cases include no benchmark names, scores, protocol, or examples. GitHub and Google have direct commercial incentives, and this is one underlying model-release announcement without independent corroboration. For this audience it is model-picker news rather than evidence of a production-ready workflow, falling under the policy’s exclusion of model-release scorekeeping without demonstrated workflow implications.","version_id":"v-9e3b7675dd5b66ce334d1e75"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"feed:independent-research-authors:258392c93310baab1471","piece_ids":["01","02","03"],"reason":"AgentSWE supplies fresh, inspectable primary evidence: 25 commissioned creation, editing, and optimization tasks; frozen submissions; held-out acceptance cases; requirement-derived rubrics; and hard gates. Its reported development-to-held-out gap, low creation/editing scores, and failure traces—visible-case overfitting, hollow runtimes, and unsupported completion—are directly relevant to production-readiness and more novel than another issue-repair benchmark. The results remain bounded to a small preprint benchmark focused on agent software, with uncertain task representativeness and repeated-run stability; the authors also benefit from establishing their benchmark as discriminating. This is independent of the vendor launches. Use 01 as a consequential counter-signal, 02 for the main evaluation, and 03 to support frozen held-out acceptance tests rather than trusting demonstrations or self-reports.","version_id":"v-b8c088105e97e9e6f3ce9ed9"},{"decision":"reject","item_id":"feed:independent-research-authors:337cbc4cedf5cfb1d758","piece_ids":[],"reason":"The new contribution is an argumentative synthesis, not a fresh empirical study. Its cited productivity, repository, and survey numbers are potentially relevant to small teams, but those claims should be checked against and attributed to the original studies; this version does not make them new evidence. Assertions that a structural vacuum or irreducible model limitations can never be removed by training go beyond the mixed empirical material summarized. The authors’ noncommercial incentive is to establish the paper’s software-engineering thesis, and the practical conclusions substantially duplicate stronger primary benchmark, supervision, and practitioner items in this set. It may serve as a source-discovery map, but not as selected evidence.","version_id":"v-e9b1abf6d3b4b6aeda723cc0"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"feed:independent-research-authors:89ac63769de00fed6835","piece_ids":["03"],"reason":"The observation and workflow-diagram study of 19 experienced developers yields a novel seven-stage supervision framework and concrete practices such as concentrating effort in planning and turning repeated guidance into reusable assets. That makes otherwise hidden oversight work legible and is directly actionable for 2–20-person teams. The qualitative sample cannot establish prevalence, causal effectiveness, or ROI, while the Reddit material is self-selected; framework authors also have an incentive to fit varied behavior into a coherent taxonomy. It complements rather than duplicates AgentSWE by studying human operating work instead of delivery scores. Use it in 03 as a planning and measurement lens, not a universal lifecycle or proven best practice.","version_id":"v-9bde3907428df8ef68a78026"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"feed:sourcegraph:32584b6ceadae8f3a512","piece_ids":["01","02","03"],"reason":"At the window boundary, this reports a materially new cross-repository workflow: scope, plan, pilot, adapt across repositories, react to CI, and retain human merge control, with scripts used for repetitive work and agents for judgment-heavy cases. Nearly 1,000 merged beta changesets, Mercari’s roughly 80 potentially affected repositories, and Canva’s 50-plus PRs are useful named observations but provide no denominator, rejection rate, defect rate, review effort, time saving, or rollback outcome. The examples are vendor-selected, not independent corroboration, and Sourcegraph sells the product under per-merged-change pricing, which may reward change volume. Enterprise-scale examples limit small-team generalization. Use 01 for the launch, 02 to distinguish adoption footprint from effectiveness, and 03 for a bounded staged pilot with CI, approval, rollback, and cost-per-accepted-change tracking.","version_id":"v-b33c45204054589dffdd9e18"},{"decision":"reject","item_id":"feed:sourcegraph:ea3179ffe2d4c95b4f7b","piece_ids":[],"reason":"The essay offers useful questions about identity, authorization, budget controls, retrieval, and narrowly scoped trigger/function workflows, but it supplies no inspectable study, named case, or artifact showing that the proposed architecture works. Assertions that prompt-to-PR is solved, model quality has plateaued, and brownfield maintenance is unsolved rest mainly on unnamed conversations and opinion. Its enterprise focus weakens relevance to small teams, and its emphasis on universal code visibility aligns directly with Sourcegraph’s commercial offering and duplicates the Batch Changes launch narrative. The constraints could inspire a watch list, but this version is too promotional and speculative to serve as evidence.","version_id":"v-1c7d0d28b27050f0e12c26c2"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"podcast:infoq:5925e1fbf36f4960a85e","piece_ids":["02","03"],"reason":"The timestamped transcript provides direct, attributable practitioner observations about ambiguous requirements, verification burden, legacy systems whose real requirements are unclear, and the need for explicit tests and retained human understanding. These are highly relevant to technical leads and add a legacy-system perspective not supplied by the benchmark or vendor announcements. They remain one experienced engineer’s judgment, with no task sample, measured failure rate, or comparison; InfoQ and the guest benefit from attention, though the excerpt shows no direct sale of a featured agent. Use 02 as qualified practitioner experience and 03 to motivate explicit requirements, assumptions, and acceptance tests—not as proof that code review generally fails.","version_id":"v-fa6a1a051450d1962bb56646"},{"decision":"reject","item_id":"podcast:infoq:5950b2ca18b6b0b75291","piece_ids":[],"reason":"Psychological safety, team alignment, and human ownership are relevant adoption concerns, but the strongest capability claim—that appropriate skills and prompts now make correctness, safety, and reliability concerns largely satisfied—has no examples, telemetry, or evaluation and conflicts with the later emphasis on verification burden. That makes the disagreement insufficiently evidenced rather than a reliable counterpoint. The episode also repeats architecture, junior-training, and oversight themes covered more concretely by the other InfoQ transcripts, so selecting it would over-weight one host and distribution channel. The guest and publisher have attention incentives; rejection is an editorial judgment on this evidence version, not on the general importance of psychological safety.","version_id":"v-dbe33bbe448ee0d2555a358e"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"podcast:infoq:d6cf9bc155dcb06cf247","piece_ids":["02","03"],"reason":"Published on the window boundary, the transcript includes a concrete first-person observation: an agent accumulated a god object over several weeks while producing features, illustrating a possible gap between local task success and architecture. The proposed nursing-style preceptor role is also a novel, relevant response to the junior-development pipeline, though it is an untested analogy rather than evidence of effectiveness. One anecdote cannot establish general agent behavior, and Hanselman’s Microsoft/GitHub affiliation plus the podcast’s attention incentive should be disclosed. It is distinct from Joy Ebertz’s requirements focus. Use 02 for the bounded architecture observation and 03 as a training experiment or watch signal, not a settled organizational prescription.","version_id":"v-6e820812bb6374c9491cabb4"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"youtube:9yPyoxlyc5Q","piece_ids":["03"],"reason":"The transcript shows a concrete workflow against a real repository and issue: structured clarification before implementation, repository guidance, visual PR explanations, and a review skill that checks coding standards through subagents. That artifact-level demonstration is more useful to small-team leads than generic prompting advice and independently illustrates the research finding that recurring supervision can become reusable assets. It does not measure quality, time, defects, or review accuracy, and repository popularity is not effectiveness evidence. The speaker promotes his skills repository while GitHub promotes Copilot, creating dual incentives. Use only in 03 as a reproducible practitioner pattern to test, not as proof that the skills improve outcomes.","version_id":"v-ab01f07d4890bf0557ad681d"},{"decision":"reject","item_id":"youtube:hTAWHgQI4xg","piece_ids":[],"reason":"The security warning and sandbox recommendation are relevant, but the video offers no inspected incident, experiment, or new control design. Claims that agent tasks formerly taking weeks or months now finish in minutes and that whole features routinely move through staging and production are unsupported by task definitions or outcomes. Most of the remaining spec, context, loop, and subagent guidance duplicates stronger research and practitioner evidence in the set. IBM benefits from brand attention around agent adoption, and the opening pilot anecdote is unverifiable. This is a broad explainer rather than production-readiness evidence.","version_id":"v-470d183469c7db5d35e05d67"},{"decision":"reject","item_id":"youtube:7XzjQa8z0uc","piece_ids":[],"reason":"This is explicitly a beginner, non-coder tutorial built around a toy cookie-shop game. It demonstrates basic Codex file editing, iteration, and Git UI, but offers no production requirements, CI, security, review, maintenance, or outcome measurement relevant to experienced technical leads. The creator benefits from tutorial attention, and the feature demonstrations depend on OpenAI’s underlying product; the two primary OpenAI videos are better evidence for those shipped capabilities. Its beginner prompting focus is expressly outside the publication’s scope, so freshness does not overcome the audience and evidence mismatch.","version_id":"v-fe38088af4757b05a5b066aa"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"youtube:IZXv6a78NDw","piece_ids":["01"],"reason":"The vendor video reports a concrete workflow change: GitHub code review is generally available in Codex, GitLab support is in preview, and users can combine automatic cloud review, GitHub comments, per-PR private chat, team skills or documents, local review, and review actions. That is consequential for small teams and distinct from Cursor’s deployment-monitoring announcement, even though both extend agents beyond code generation. OpenAI has a direct commercial incentive, and the title’s claim that review is no longer a bottleneck is unsupported—there are no precision, false-positive, defect, throughput, or reviewer-effort results. Use 01 only for availability and workflow scope, not effectiveness.","version_id":"v-aa6fb499336c3701ec05174c"},{"decision":"accept","item_id":"youtube:PUBc2G0Tj5E","piece_ids":["01"],"reason":"The primary vendor demonstration supplies specific evidence of what changed in the CLI: a full-screen task interface, three parallel tasks across projects, status and follow-up controls, worktree-based conversation forks, remote mobile control, usage analytics, and rendered diagrams. These orchestration and isolation features have direct workflow relevance for small teams, but the staged demo provides no evidence about completion quality, merge rate, coordination failures, cost, or remote-control security. OpenAI’s commercial incentive requires limiting claims to demonstrated interface capabilities. This substantially overlaps the beginner Codex tutorial at the feature level, so the primary source is retained and the tutorial rejected.","version_id":"v-f95ed73f67d6b610264834f4"},{"decision":"defer","item_id":"youtube:J9NQTYUP6k0","piece_ids":[],"reason":"The transcript contains potentially useful, current operational claims about plan mode, verification criteria, goal-loop judging, effort settings, and instruction reduction. However, its important claims—including a two-to-three-times quality gain, deletion of more than 80% of instructions, and descriptions of Anthropic or Boris Cherny guidance—depend on primary posts and documentation that are not linked or inspectable in this evidence version. The creator also promotes a paid course, and the top-1% framing rewards novelty and attention. Defer until the cited primary passages, applicable product versions, and numerical methods can be verified, or an independent reproduction tests the advice; only then could it support 02 or 03.","version_id":"v-8bb3472c3858254a3ab9d00e"}]}
